summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of kidney transplant rejection was admitted for evaluation of a positive tuberculin skin test and a several-week history of non-productive cough. Chest imaging showed chronic interstitial changes without acute findings or cavitary lesions. Three sputum samples were collected, all with negative acid-fast bacilli smears, making active tuberculosis unlikely. The patient remained stable throughout the admission, with no fever, night sweats, or other systemic symptoms. Hemodialysis was performed as scheduled. He was discharged home with plans to follow up in the infectious disease clinic in two weeks to review pending sputum and blood culture results and determine if treatment for latent tuberculosis is needed. No medication changes were made during the hospitalization.
